fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds for a Construction Job
fields.features_subheading: Each part handles one handoff between the office and the site, and every record lands on the same job.
fields.feature_1:
A due date on every RFI

Each RFI gets a number, an owner on the design team, and a running day count. Pick how many days it can sit unanswered before the project manager gets a direct message about it.
fields.feature_2:
Change orders routed by their amount

Price a change order once, with materials and labor on separate lines. The app sends it to the project manager or the owner's representative based on the dollar limits you set.
fields.feature_3:
A daily log filed from the site

The superintendent enters each crew's headcount and any delay on a phone, with photos attached. Each log is saved to its job and date, and a long delay reaches the project manager.
fields.feature_4:
AI reads subcontractor invoices

An AI step pulls the amount due and the subcontract value off each subcontractor invoice. A person checks any field the AI is unsure of before the invoice moves to approval.
fields.feature_5:
One board for every open job

The dashboard lists every open item by job, with late RFIs and held invoices at the top. It updates as the field submits, and the Monday meeting starts from current numbers.
fields.feature_6:
The job app's code, in your GitHub

Export the full code of the construction app to your GitHub repository on paid plans. The code shows how each approval is stored, and anyone can extend it like any other codebase.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Handoffs Where Construction Jobs Stall
fields.tab_content_1:
When an RFI sits 5 days, the project manager hears

Rookwell Builders has 14 open RFIs on the Fenwick Lane clinic job. Any RFI with no answer from the architect after 5 days goes to the project manager. RFI 23, on the stair door hardware, went to Corwin Ellisand 6 days ago. Talulah Brennecke, the project manager, now has a direct message naming it.
fields.tab_content_2:
Every change order over $5,000 needs the owner's approval

Odalys Pemberthy at Sabledown Contracting prices change order CO-09 for added steel lintels: $5,260 in materials and $2,580 in labor, $7,840 in all. Anything over $5,000 needs the owner's representative before work starts. Benedikt Oyelaran gets the request by email, with both cost lines attached.
fields.tab_content_3:
After a 2-hour rain delay, the project manager gets the log

Ingemar Dufresne, superintendent for Brackenmoor Construction, files the daily log from his phone. Today's log lists 22 workers in 3 crews: 10 framing, 8 electrical, and 4 plumbing, plus a 2-hour rain delay and 4 photos. Any delay over 1 hour goes to the project manager, Isandro Kowalczyk, by direct message.
fields.tab_content_4:
$48,600 billed on $42,100 of work in place is held

Halvern Electric bills Tollerton Builders $48,600 this month on its $81,000 subcontract. The app reads the invoice and compares it with the $42,100 of work in place the project manager recorded. A bill more than $2,500 over that figure is held for Wynfrith Calloway to review before accounts payable sees it.

fields.howto_description: Seven steps to turn your job's handoffs into construction workflow automation with clear limits, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List the handoffs that stall a job
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Set the day counts and dollar limits
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Describe the app in one prompt
fields.howto_step_1_des: List the handoffs that stall your jobs, such as RFIs waiting on the design team or subcontractor invoices that need a site check before payment. Next to each, write who has to answer it and how many days it sits today.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Pick the numbers each rule runs on. Decide how many days an RFI can sit before the project manager hears and which change order amount needs the owner. Then set how far a bill can run past the work in place before it is held.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write one prompt that names each record and the rules it follows, such as an RFI that needs an answer within 5 days. Emergent builds the app and its database from that description, and you change either one by prompting again.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Connect your accounting system, such as QuickBooks, through its API. Approved change orders and subcontractor invoices then reach accounting without retyping. Add Slack or email for the messages each rule sends, and name the person who receives each one.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Open the daily log on a superintendent's phone and keep it to what fits the end of a shift: the headcount for each crew and any delay with its photos. Every field you add is one more thing someone types while standing on site.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Run one job on the app first
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run one active job on the app for 2 weeks next to your current process. Compare the items it flagged with the ones your team caught by hand, and adjust a limit wherever the two lists disagree.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Add jobs one at a time
fields.howto_step_7_des: Add the next job once the first one runs clean, and move a limit when a job needs a different one. Review the open-item board in the weekly project meeting, and give every late RFI and held invoice a name.

faq_plan.a: Construction workflow automation is software that moves a job's paperwork between the office and the field by rules you set. It sends each RFI, change order, daily log, and subcontractor invoice to the right person, counts the days each one waits, and alerts someone when an item passes its limit.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up construction workflow automation?
faq_plan.a: Start with one job and the records it trades most often. Write down the limit for each, such as 5 days for an RFI answer or $5,000 for a change order. In Emergent's AI automation builder, you describe those records and limits in a prompt and get a working app with its database.

faq_plan.q: What should construction workflow automation handle first?
faq_plan.a: Start with the record your team spends the most time chasing. Count last month's items of each type and note how many waited past the limit you would set. The record with the most late items goes first. Leave approvals that happen once or twice a year on email.

faq_plan.q: Can construction workflow automation track material deliveries to a site?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Give each delivery a record tied to its purchase order, with the expected date and the person on site who signs for it. If your carrier offers a tracking API, the app can read the status and message the superintendent the day before arrival. Shipping automation applies the same tracking logic to outbound orders.

faq_plan.q: How does construction workflow automation get superintendents to file daily logs?
faq_plan.a: It sends a reminder at the end of each shift to any superintendent who has not filed, and lists missing logs by name on the weekly board. Keep the log short enough to finish on a phone in 5 minutes, and prefill the crews from the day before.

faq_plan.q: How does construction workflow automation connect to accounting software?
faq_plan.a: It connects through the accounting system's API. Emergent builds apps that connect to any tool with an API and sync data in and out. Approved change orders can update the job budget, and approved subcontractor invoices can arrive as bills that nobody types twice.

faq_plan.q: Can construction workflow automation share data with an online store?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when both write to the same database. A contractor that also sells fixtures or materials online can keep store orders and job records side by side, and reserve a stocked item for a job when it sells. The store side is ecommerce automation, and its alerts follow the same pattern as the job alerts.

faq_plan.q: How do I measure whether construction workflow automation saves time?
faq_plan.a: Measure how long items wait, not how many clicks they take. Before you switch, record the average number of days each type of record sat last month. After a month on the app, compare the same averages and the count of items that passed their limit. Every record carries its dates, and the dashboard shows both months.

faq_plan.q: How do I keep subcontractor paperwork current in construction workflow automation?
faq_plan.a: Give each subcontractor one record that holds every document you collect from them, with its expiry date. Send a reminder 30 days before a date passes, and hold new invoices from anyone whose document has lapsed until it is replaced. In an app built with Emergent, those records live in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Can construction workflow automation check material orders against a job budget?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Tie every material request to a job and a cost code, and the app checks it against what is left in that code before it reaches the supplier. Requests within budget go to purchasing; anything over goes to the project manager first. That request-to-order path is procurement automation, and it draws on the same job budget as your change orders.

plan.angle: Construction software vendors rank with feature lists for one product. This page shows the four office-to-field handoffs a contractor can automate with an app it owns: RFIs that wait on the architect, change orders routed by amount, a daily log filed from a phone, and a subcontractor invoice checked against the percent complete the project manager recorded. The FAQ covers where to start, deliveries, accounting, paperwork and measuring the result, as plain operator advice with no safety or legal claims.
